source_title: Contrastive Somali Grammar for Mother Tongue Speakers
attested_fact: The grammar gives exact feminine singular Gabadhu with separated waa ay and feminine finite ordaysaa.
linguistic_interpretation: The source explicitly states that noun gender determines the choice of uu/ay and the verb suffix when the noun is the subject.
project_rule_relevance: The project already reviews exact Gabadhu as feminine singular, but noun_gender_agreement currently only scans contracted wuu/way after the noun.
test_expectation: The noun-gender analyzer should recognize the separated waa ay realization as the same reviewed third-person feminine statement-clitic family without requiring a fused spelling.
training_evaluation_usefulness: Positive holdout for spacing/contraction robustness in noun-gender agreement.
proves: Exact separated waa ay is licensed with reviewed feminine noun subject Gabadhu and feminine verb ordaysaa in this source.
does_not_prove: It does not license arbitrary waa + pronoun sequences, infer gender for unknown nouns, or establish unseen verb paradigms.

source_title: Contrastive Somali Grammar for Mother Tongue Speakers
attested_fact: The grammar gives exact masculine singular Wiilku with separated waa uu and masculine finite ordayaa.
linguistic_interpretation: The source explicitly contrasts this sentence with feminine Gabadhu waa ay ordaysaa to demonstrate noun-gender agreement.
project_rule_relevance: The project already reviews exact Wiilku as masculine singular; this tests an independently attested surface realization not covered by the noun-gender scanner.
test_expectation: The noun-gender analyzer should recognize separated waa uu for the already-reviewed masculine singular subject without inventing morphology.
training_evaluation_usefulness: Positive minimal-pair holdout for masculine noun agreement under uncontracted statement marking.
proves: Exact separated waa uu is licensed with Wiilku and ordayaa in this source.
does_not_prove: It does not license arbitrary subject nouns or generate new finite forms.

source_title: Contrastive Somali Grammar for Mother Tongue Speakers
attested_fact: The grammar explicitly analyzes fused wuu as corresponding to separated waa uu.
linguistic_interpretation: Spacing/fusion must not erase the underlying statement particle plus short subject pronoun analysis.
project_rule_relevance: Supports treating exact waa uu and waa ay as uncontracted realizations of the already-reviewed statement-clitic construction rather than as a new paradigm.
test_expectation: Agreement checking should be equivalent across fused and separated realizations when the noun subject itself is already reviewed.
training_evaluation_usefulness: Equivalence test for orthographic realization versus grammatical function.
proves: Explicit equivalence of wuu and waa uu in the cited construction.
does_not_prove: It does not justify normalizing all spacing automatically or accepting unattested clitic combinations.

source: Morgan Nilsson, Contrastive Somali Grammar for Mother Tongue Speakers, p. 175
linguistic_interpretation: Crossing the masculine uu/ordayaa agreement set onto the reviewed feminine singular subject creates the gender mismatch that the source's contrast teaches.
test_expectation: The checker should report a noun-subject gender/clitic conflict; this sentence is a QA minimal pair, not an attested corpus sentence.
training_evaluation_usefulness: Negative minimal pair for false-negative detection.
proves: Nothing about attestation; it is deliberately constructed only from independently attested components to test the stated agreement contrast.
does_not_prove: It is not evidence that speakers actually produce this sentence.

source_title: Contrastive Somali Grammar for Mother Tongue Speakers
source_rule: A definite noun used as an unfocused subject changes final -a to subject -u; the grammar gives Wiilku waa uu kacayaa and Wiilku waa uu ordayaa.
test_expectation: The noun-subject-case analyzer should flag Wiilka before separated waa uu and identify Wiilku as the reviewed subject-form candidate.
training_evaluation_usefulness: Negative case minimal pair testing that spacing of the statement particle does not disable subject-case checking.
proves: The cited source backs the subject -u rule and exact Wiilku + waa uu construction; this malformed QA sentence is not an attestation.
does_not_prove: It does not justify rewriting unknown noun forms by suffix analogy.
